newsitem.title: CHINA: Weakening Typhoon Victor spares HK major damage.
newsitem.headline: Weakening Typhoon Victor spares HK major damage.

text.p: Hong Kong battened down the hatches on Saturday as Typhoon Victor swept across the territory, but appeared to escape serious damage as the winds eased.
Weather forecasters said Victor was weakening into a "severe tropical storm" as it moved north across Hong Kong towards China's frontier city of Shenzhen.

The Hong Kong Observatory said it would not issue the rarely-used super typhoon "10" signal as feared earlier on Saturday, stopping instead at number nine, which indicates winds of more than 118 km per hour (73 mph).
The tropical cyclone severely disrupted air, land and sea traffic, closed businesses early and sent residents rushing to stock up with food ahead of what threatened to be a turbulent night.

Traffic snarled as people headed home to barricade doors and windows against Typhoon Victor, which had been expected to be the most destructive to hit the territory since 1983. Soon after city centre streets resembled a ghost town.
Despite the easing of Victor's force, strong winds and heavy rains would continue to batter the territory, the forecasters said, advising its 6.4 million people to stay indoors.
The densely-populated Portuguese colony of Macau also hoisted the number nine warning signal.

More than 180 flights due to leave or arrive in Hong Kong were diverted, delayed or cancelled. Ferry services to outlying islands and to Macau were cancelled. Victoria Harbour, one of the world's busiest, was emptied as ships docked in typhoon shelters.

Bus and railway services were suspended, while the underground rail system provided limited service. The huge Tsing Ma suspension bridge, which links Lantau Island to the Kowloon peninsula, was closed because of the danger from strong winds.

But initial reports from the Hong Kong government suggested only minor incidents of landslips, floodings and trees being toppled. Some 32 people suffered minor injuries and three were rescued after being swept away by waves while sitting at bars next to Hong Kong island's Stanley beach, the government said.
Macau's small international airport was closed and bus services were also shut down.
Victor was the most powerful typhoon to approach Hong Kong since Typhoon Ellen in 1983, which caused serious damage.
